bool valid_arguments(const ToolDefinition& definition, const json& arguments)
{
    if (!arguments.is_object())
        return false;

    if (definition.handler == ToolHandler::SettingsSearch)
        return has_only(arguments, {"query", "limit", "cursor"}) && arguments.contains("query") &&
               arguments["query"].is_string() && optional_string(arguments, "cursor") &&
               (!arguments.contains("limit") || (arguments["limit"].is_number_unsigned() &&
                 arguments["limit"].get<std::uint64_t>() >= 1 && arguments["limit"].get<std::uint64_t>() <= 25));
    if (definition.handler == ToolHandler::SettingsGet) {
        if (!has_only(arguments, {"keys"}) || !arguments.contains("keys") || !arguments["keys"].is_array() ||
            arguments["keys"].empty() || arguments["keys"].size() > 32)
            return false;
        return std::all_of(arguments["keys"].begin(), arguments["keys"].end(), [](const auto& key) { return key.is_string(); });
    }
    if (definition.handler == ToolHandler::SettingsPreviewPatch || definition.handler == ToolHandler::SettingsApplyPatch) {
        const bool apply = definition.handler == ToolHandler::SettingsApplyPatch;
        if (!(apply ? has_only(arguments, {"changes", "expectedSessionId", "expectedRevision", "intent"}) : has_only(arguments, {"changes"})) ||
            !arguments.contains("changes") || !arguments["changes"].is_object() || arguments["changes"].empty() ||
            arguments["changes"].size() > 32)
            return false;
        if (apply && (!arguments.contains("expectedSessionId") || !is_unsigned_string(arguments["expectedSessionId"]) ||
                      !arguments.contains("expectedRevision") || !arguments["expectedRevision"].is_number_unsigned()))
            return false;
        if (apply && !optional_string(arguments, "intent"))
            return false;
        return std::all_of(arguments["changes"].begin(), arguments["changes"].end(), [](const auto& value) {
            return value.is_string() || value.is_number() || value.is_boolean();
        });

function(jusprin_web_bundle name project_dir output)
    file(GLOB_RECURSE _src CONFIGURE_DEPENDS ${project_dir}/src/*)
    set(_stamp ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/${name}-node_modules.stamp)
    # npm ci writes node_modules/.package-lock.json. Listing it as OUTPUT
    # means deleting node_modules retriggers the install; the stamp in the
    # build tree is what the bundle command depends on.
    set(_modules ${project_dir}/node_modules/.package-lock.json)
    add_custom_command(OUTPUT ${_stamp} ${_modules}
        COMMAND ${JUSPRIN_NPM} ci --no-audit --no-fund
        COMMAND ${CMAKE_COMMAND} -E touch ${_stamp}
        DEPENDS ${project_dir}/package.json ${project_dir}/package-lock.json
        WORKING_DIRECTORY ${project_dir}
        COMMENT "npm ci (${name})"
        VERBATIM)
    add_custom_command(OUTPUT ${output}
        COMMAND ${JUSPRIN_NPM} run build
        DEPENDS ${_stamp} ${_src} ${_jusprin_web_shared_inputs}
                ${project_dir}/index.html ${project_dir}/vite.config.ts ${project_dir}/tsconfig.json
        WORKING_DIRECTORY ${project_dir}
        COMMENT "vite build (${name}) -> ${output}"
        VERBATIM)
endfunction()

=== guide catalog record section ===
## Catalog record

Current registry, in deterministic name order. `Internal` entries are native manufacturing-history commands, not AI tools:

| Tool | Added for eval/task | Action | Exposure | Scope | Owner | Output bound |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `duplicate_object` | Duplicate a project object | mutation | in-app | one explicit session-scoped object ID, not necessarily selected | `IWorkspace::duplicate_object` | revision and optional new object ID |
| `import_model` | Add a user attachment | mutation | in-app | current document; importable attachment required | `IWorkspace::import_model` | revision, imported flag and optional new object ID |
| `inspect_selection` | Explain selected geometry | read-only | in-app | current selection | workspace snapshot | at most 64 names, each at most 256 UTF-8 bytes; revision and conditional truncation flag |
| `record_build` | Record a sliced plate | mutation | Internal | manufacturing history | coordinator's history recorder | build ID and recorded flag |
| `record_export_copy` | Record a verified G-code export | destructive | Internal | manufacturing history | coordinator's history recorder | exported-copy ID and build ID |
| `record_physical_print` | Record a completed print fact | destructive | Internal | manufacturing history; does not start a printer | coordinator's history recorder | physical-print ID, build ID and recorded flag |
| `settings_apply_patch` | Apply the approved batch without overwriting a newer edit | mutation | both | preview session/revision and confirmed before/after values | `IWorkspace::apply_settings` through `Tab::load_config` | bounded actual changes/normalization, revision, dirty flag and `projectUndo: false` |
| `settings_get` | Read current values and preset origin | read-only | both | 1–32 process keys | `IWorkspace::read_settings` using the edited process preset | at most 32 values and unknown-key issues; canonical values are preserved |
| `settings_preview_patch` | Check a batch before requesting approval | read-only | both | active FFF process preset; seven writable keys | `IWorkspace::preview_settings` using a clone and Orca validation/normalization | at most 32 input keys; bounded changes, dependencies, issues and warnings |
| `settings_search` | Find a process setting without loading its full catalog | read-only | both | active FFF process preset | `IWorkspace::search_settings` using Orca definitions | 1–25 matches; deterministic cursor paging and bounded metadata |
| `workspace_inspect` | Client needs current project context | read-only | both | current document | `IWorkspace::snapshot` | at most 16 plates, 64 objects across returned plates and 64 selected IDs; labels at most 256 UTF-8 bytes; totals and truncation flags |

Only `workspace_inspect`, `settings_search`, `settings_get`, `settings_preview_patch`, and `settings_apply_patch` are MCP-visible. `duplicate_object` and `inspect_selection` remain in-app fixtures pending an in-app eval; they are not callable over MCP. There is no MCP attachment-import contract.

Settings search/read cover the active FFF process preset. The write allowlist is `layer_height`, `wall_loops`, `sparse_infill_density`, `sparse_infill_pattern`, `top_shell_layers`, `bottom_shell_layers`, and `brim_width`. Apply takes `changes`, `expectedSessionId`, and `expectedRevision` from a fresh preview. Native approval captures the exact before/after values, including normalization dependencies, then revalidates before applying. It publishes one `Settings` revision, updates native fields and dirty state, and invalidates slicing. Use Orca preset revert or a previewed inverse patch to restore values; ordinary project Undo does not reverse preset edits.

The OpenAI adapter preserves the registry schemas and uses non-strict function calling for optional arguments or dynamic patch maps, which OpenAI strict mode cannot express. Native registry validation remains authoritative. Stateless Responses continuations retain user context and all prior tool results; the live multi-tool regression covers this path.

Update the actual table when implementation changes names, limits, or ownership. The source registry remains authoritative; this table explains why the surface exists.

## Process-settings tools: contract and hazards

The settings tools are the reference implementation of this guide. What
follows is the part of their design that stays true after the work is done;
the implementation handoff that produced it is retired. Re-read this section
before expanding the write allowlist or adding a tool that changes a preset.

content.text:
Pulled: `jusprin-newui` fast-forwarded 18 commits to `5fc0efe2e3`, clean tree.

**No — three things are missing, and one of them blocks M0 on day one.**

## 1. The guide the handoff defers to doesn't contain the parts it defers to

The handoff says "the rules live in [the tool extension guide] … when this document and the guide disagree, the guide wins." The guide in the repo ([mcp-tool-extension-guide.md](agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md), 514 lines, last touched by `9e772ec46c`) has **none** of the sections the handoff cites as normative. Zero matches, in the working tree and across every ref's history:

| Handoff cites | In the guide |
|---|---|
| "the guide's candidate catalog" — names + contracts for the 27 new tools | absent |
| "Tool budget and tool shape" | absent |
| "Computation-only mutations" (M0) | absent |
| "JusPrin-owned project state" + provenance vocabulary (M0) | absent |
| "Image results" (M6) | absent |
| "Grouped approvals" / `planId` (M7) | absent |
| "Deliberately not tools" (the scope boundary) | absent |

What the guide *does* have is the "Catalog record" table for the 11 entries that exist today (5 MCP tools, 3 in-app fixtures, 3 internal `record_*`). So the handoff's hardest rule — "Names and contracts come from the candidate catalog. Do not invent new names." — points at a document that isn't here. I can't write `object_analyze`'s section list, `slice_report`'s sections, `region_annotate`'s semantic kinds, or the provenance vocabulary without either that text or your permission to author it.

## 2. Two pointers in the handoff have drifted from the code

- **The live regression isn't where the handoff says.** `tests/agent/test_agent_bridge.cpp` has no live test. The live multi-tool path is the shell harness: [shell_harness.cpp:3557](tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp:3557) `--live-agent`, and it takes the key from `OPENAI_API_KEY` in the environment ([:3560](tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp:3560)), not "the key stored in AppConfig" (the *app's* key moved to AppConfig in `c2f28ff8c7`; the harness didn't follow).
- **M0 conflates two enums.** `ProjectStateChangeReason` is [ProjectState.hpp:16](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Workspace/ProjectState.hpp:16); `kInvalidatingReasons` is a `WorkspaceChangeReasons` mask at [ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:22](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Agent/ToolExecutionCoordinator.cpp:22). Adding `Intent`/`Plan` to the invalidating set as written would make the agent's own `intent_update` fail its own pending proposals with `stale_revision` — that needs a decision, not a guess.

Everything else I spot-checked is accurate: `outputSchema` is emitted at [McpProtocol.cpp:208](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Mcp/McpProtocol.cpp:208); the schema matcher supports only `type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/minimum/maxItems` and **throws** on anything else, so `enum`/`maxLength` really is a prerequisite; `FakeWorkspace.hpp` is now in `tests/jusprin_support/` where the handoff's links expect it. One cost the handoff doesn't price: input validation is hand-written per handler in `valid_arguments`, not schema-driven — 27 tools means 27 hand-written validators plus `ToolHandler` entries.

## 3. This machine cannot run the verification the handoff requires

- **No Node/npm and no Python 3.** Both absent. Node is now fatal: the commit I just pulled (`5fc0efe2e3`) deletes the checked-in `resources/jusprin/{agent,home}/index.html` and makes configure `FATAL_ERROR` without npm ([Web/CMakeLists.txt](src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Web/CMakeLists.txt)). `-DJUSPRIN_BUILD_WEB=OFF` is no longer a fallback — there's no prebuilt bundle left to supply. **Every in-app eval (M1–M7 and final eval 1) and every real-MCP-client transcript is blocked until Node is installed.** No Python blocks `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests/mcp`, which the handoff requires per tool.
- **No `OPENAI_API_KEY`**, so the live transcripts and the token/cache numbers that the deferral decision depends on can't be produced.
- The build tree is pre-pull (Sep 13): `orca-slicer.exe`, `jusprin-mcp.exe`, `agent_bridge_tests.exe` are stale and there's no shell-harness binary. Headless GL is fine — `Testing/windows-gl/provision-mesa-windows.ps1` is in place.
- The offline catalog-size recipe is a macOS path and needs python3; I'd rewrite it for Windows, and re-measure the 9,723-byte baseline on the build I'm comparing against rather than trusting a number taken on the macOS binary.

What I *can* do here today: `agent_bridge_tests` doesn't depend on the web bundle, so the registry, decoder, fake-workspace, and coordinator layers of M0 build and run on this box. The real-adapter, shell, and MCP-client layers do not.

## What I need from you

1. The updated guide with the candidate catalog — or explicit permission to author the catalog and the six missing sections into the guide as the first PR, which the handoff currently forbids.
2. Node LTS and Python 3 on this machine, plus an `OPENAI_API_KEY`.
3. Your two open items, which you already flagged: image projection timing for `project_attachment_read`/`view_render` in M6, and how far the M4 allowlist goes past support/adhesion/seam/wall/infill/shell.
